item.title: Boosie Badazz Gets Baby No. 10 News In Rajel Nelson’s Birthday Surprise
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Boosie Badazz and Rajel Nelson are expecting their second child together after she shares an early birthday pregnancy reveal.
item.content:encoded:
Boosie Badazz is expecting his tenth child after Rajel Nelson turned an early birthday gift into a pregnancy reveal. The couple are preparing for their second baby together.

Nelson shared the surprise on her Instagram page November 11.

“It’s a early birthday surprise 🤭💜,” she wrote alongside the video.

The clip shows a custom golf cart with “Boosie Network” across the windshield and a large red bow. Nelson also hands Boosie a package, giving him something else to open beside his new ride.

A pregnancy test appears in a blue presentation box during the video. 

The reveal included a baby onesie bearing the message, “You can stop asking now.”

View this post on Instagram

For Boosie, another baby follows a plan he had been discussing before the couple welcomed their first daughter.

In November 2024, AllHipHop covered his wish for a tenth child while Nelson was still pregnant with his ninth.

The couple welcomed daughter Sevyn Emerald in April 2025. AllHipHop’s coverage at the time documented Boosie’s emotional response to becoming a father again.

His growing family already includes children who have followed him into music. Daughter Iviona performs as Poison Ivi, while son Torrence Jr. is known as Tootie Raww.

His other children include Ivy Ray, Lyric Beyonce, Toriana, Michael Jordan, Tarlaysia and Laila Jean.

The family has also faced difficult public moments. His son Ivy Ray Hatch, then 18, was arrested October 22 in Livingston Parish, Louisiana, on charges including armed robbery and aggravated second-degree battery, WBRZ reported, citing deputies.

Hatch was released that night on $275,500 bond. Boosie later denied the robbery allegation, describing the incident as a fight.

Separately, his adult daughter Iviona publicly objected in September 2024 to his repeated comments about her being gay.

She described the hurt those public remarks caused, according to AllHipHop’s contemporaneous coverage.

Boosie subsequently apologized publicly and asked for forgiveness. “YO DADDY TRULY SORRY N I HOPE U CAN FORGIVE ME,” he wrote.

Nelson posted the new pregnancy reveal on November 11.

item.title: Ole Miss Racist Video Fallout Grows As Fundraiser Opposes Apology
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Alaina Kunes has left Ole Miss as a fundraiser for another woman in the racist video threatens cancellation over an apology.
item.content:encoded:
Alaina Kunes has left Ole Miss after the racist doorbell video outside Black students’ apartment sparked outrage, while a fundraiser for another woman identified in the incident is pushing in the opposite direction: no apology.

A spokesperson for Kunes’ lawyer told the New York Post that the 18-year-old voluntarily withdrew and was not suspended or asked to leave. The spokesperson did not disclose when she withdrew or why.

Victoria Johnson’s mother told CBS Mornings: “I hate to hear that, but I feel like everybody needs to be accountable.”

The development follows the doorbell footage previously reported by AllHipHop, which showed monkey noises and gestures outside an apartment shared by Black Ole Miss students. The November 6 incident prompted a university investigation.

Kunes apologized in a November 10 statement released by her law firm, Gardiner Koch Weisberg & Wrona.

“To the women I offended and to the Ole Miss community, I sincerely apologize,” she said.

She maintained she had not known the residents’ race before the incident, acknowledged that her conduct caused harm and pledged to cooperate with the university’s investigation.

Meanwhile, a GiveSendGo campaign titled “Stand with Lauren” identifies Lauren Mayfield as another woman in the footage. Its creator, Tom Hennessey, says donations are intended to help with lost income and opportunities. His campaign description defends her conduct and discourages an apology.

“I reserve the right to cancel this fundraiser if Lauren disavows our support and bends the knee,” Hennessey wrote.

That condition is the organizer’s statement, not a statement from Mayfield. The campaign page does not establish that she has accepted its money or endorsed his message.

The university’s response has centered on the students targeted and its disciplinary process. In a November 8 campus message, Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs Shawnboda Mead condemned the conduct and said staff had contacted the affected students to offer support.

Mead said the Office of Conflict Resolution and Student Conduct and Equal Opportunity and Regulatory Compliance were investigating. Federal privacy protections limit what the university can disclose about individual disciplinary matters.

The university also warned that one student had been incorrectly identified online and said no members of its sorority community were involved.

item.title: Tyler, The Creator Gives Converse's Bronco Boot A Low-Top Makeover
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Tyler, The Creator's next Converse drop brings a $130 low-cut Bronco with boot hardware and a November 12 release.
item.content:encoded:
Tyler The Creator has a $130 answer for anyone who wants boot details without a boot climbing their ankle. His new Converse Bronco Boot Low puts that lower cut at the center of the latest GOLF le FLEUR* offering.

The shoe keeps the chunky hardware while changing the proportions around it. Converse's official launch page lists leather construction, a rubber toe drawn from its archives and a welted lug outsole.

Metal hardware gives the low-profile shape another connection to the boot world. The U.S. collection page lists Cocoa Brown/Rubber, Eden/Rubber and Black/Vanilla Ice versions, with a New Wheat Bronco Ox also priced at $130.

That archive connection has been part of Tyler's pitch from the beginning. In Converse's May 2025 "Tyler Talk: London" interview, he explained how asking to see the company's older designs led him beyond its familiar Chucks.

He described finding 1970s running shoes and boat shoes that deserved another look. Rather than starting with a blank page, he wanted to change colors and update shapes already sitting inside the company. He said he'd asked Converse to send material from its earliest years so he could work through the full range.

"Again, it's just having people around you that trust you and if you have a crazy idea, they'll help you facilitate it," Tyler said. He was discussing the collaborators who helped turn those archived designs into shoes people could actually wear.

The new Bronco arrives during another busy stretch for Tyler's work outside the recording studio. His separate GOLF WANG brand recently took over FC Barcelona's Clásico shirt campaign, with creative control over the graphics and video.

That project extended into an 11-piece clothing collection and a cultural space in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. With Converse, the focus returns to footwear and the design history that first caught his attention in those archive sessions.

The collection page also lists a Golden Haze/Yarrow/Tan Jogger for the November 12 launch. That gives the release a running-shoe option alongside the Bronco shapes featured in the new presentation.

Converse's U.S. product listing sets the Bronco Boot Low release for November 12 at 10 a.m. Eastern.

item.title: Kai Cenat’s Company Faces Court Questions Over Two LLCs In Audition Suit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kai Cenat's New York company must explain two LLCs' roles in an audition lawsuit under a federal judge's latest order.
item.content:encoded:
Kai Cenat‘s New York company has to explain how two businesses sharing his name fit into a federal lawsuit.

A Manhattan judge wants that answer in writing as a dispute tied to Streamer University auditions moves through court.

The question isn’t whether the streamer owes anybody money, but which company belongs in the case and why.

In a November 5 order, U.S. Magistrate Judge Robert W. Lehrburger gave the New York company’s lawyer until November 12 to explain both entities’ connections to the events alleged.

That means addressing Kai Cenat LLC in New York and Kai Cenat LLC in Georgia separately. The lawyer also has to clarify whether the same legal team represents the Georgia business, rather than leaving that relationship unclear on the record.

Lehrburger also put a limit on plaintiff Caleb Gottfried’s repeated revisions: “Having already filed his Fourth Amended Complaint, Plaintiff shall not file any further amended complaints without obtaining leave of court.”

Any further rewrite now needs the judge’s permission before it can be filed.

Gottfried brought the case against Night Media and Kai Cenat LLC in June, and the New York company and Night Media filed answers in August.

His lawsuit concerns alleged crowd-safety problems at a Streamer University event, not the program’s 2025 closing ceremony that featured a surprise message from Drake.

The Georgia company’s role has been working its way through the paperwork for weeks.

On September 25, Lehrburger directed the court clerk to prepare service documents for that entity through the U.S. Marshals Service, with Gottfried responsible for making sure service happened within 90 days after the summons was issued.

An October 21 order then allowed Gottfried to submit his fourth amended complaint after the defendants didn’t respond to that request.

Lehrburger also declined his request for a free lawyer at that stage, while allowing him to ask again later as the case develops.

That request covered help with depositions and trial, and the judge considered it premature before the defendants answered or any motions to dismiss were resolved.

The November 5 order sets those next steps without deciding whether either company is liable.

item.title: Quavo’s ‘Bubble Gum’ Case Moves Toward Settlement With Music Giants
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Quavo's music companies reach a deal with L.Mont over "Bubble Gum," with lawyers asking for time to finish the agreement.
item.content:encoded:
Quavo could soon put the “Bubble Gum” copyright fight behind him but the deal still needs to be finished. A new court filing puts the music companies and the rapper who sued them on a 40-day path toward wrapping things up.

The November 11 joint notice says L.Mont has reached a settlement in principle with UMG Recordings, Universal Music-MGB and Warner-Tamerlane Publishing. Those companies joined his request to clear the court’s calendar while they complete the agreement.

“The Plaintiff and Defendants, therefore, apply to this Honorable Court to vacate all currently set dates with the expectation that the settlement will be consummated within forty (40) days,” their lawyers wrote. The notice doesn’t disclose a payment amount or spell out the settlement’s other terms.

There’s a distinction here for Quavo, whose name remains in the case caption. The notice identifies the corporate defendants as the settling parties, rather than listing him among that group, and isn’t itself a dismissal order.

L.Mont’s September 15 amended complaint traces the dispute to February 9, 2016. He says he opened for Migos and 2 Chainz at New Orleans’ Saenger Theatre, then handed Quavo a demo at the VLive after-party.

The songwriter says he created “Bubblegum” in 2015 and included it on that CD, hoping to collaborate. He alleges Quavo accepted the disc and said he would consider the request, then used protected elements without permission.

“There are unmistakable similarities between the two works,” the amended complaint states. L.Mont alleges similarities in lyrics, melody and arrangement, not just the title. The complaint adds: “Moreover, both songs have the similar tempos and form structure.” L.Mont also seeks songwriting credit on awards or other recognition tied to the track, alongside damages, profits and an injunction. Those are allegations and demands, not findings of infringement.

The challenged song appeared on Quavo Huncho, long before the rapper’s latest plans for more solo music and Migos recordings. The proposed agreement addresses that older catalog dispute while his recording career keeps moving.

Warner-Tamerlane also used the notice to clarify that the lawsuit had incorrectly named it as W Chappell Music Corp.

item.title: GloRilla Refuses To Let Gospel Critics Silence Her Praise
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: GloRilla answers criticism of her gospel collaborations by turning to scripture and refusing to apologize for her faith.
item.content:encoded:
GloRilla says she won’t stop praising God just because critics object to her place in gospel music.

The Memphis rapper addressed the continuing complaints about her faith on Wednesday without naming an individual critic or apologizing for her work with Kirk Franklin.

In her November 11 post on X, GloRilla questioned why her praise bothers people and pointed to Psalm 150:6. Her biblical reference calls for every breathing thing to praise God.

“Long as I’m breathing ima give God the glory and nobody can ever make me feel bad about that,” GloRilla wrote.

Her response keeps the focus on her own relationship with God rather than defending every song in her catalog.

She didn’t announce a change in musical direction or withdraw from the collaborations that have drawn criticism from religious listeners.

Franklin had already defended GloRilla against that backlash during an October conversation with Big Boy.

He described the treatment as painful and rejected the suggestion that her success in mainstream rap should disqualify her from recording a gospel song.

During that interview, Franklin recalled GloRilla asking why she couldn’t praise God when scripture described even rocks doing so. He also challenged the idea that she needed a gospel feature for a financial boost, pointing to the career she’d already built outside his genre.

That discussion wasn’t limited to GloRilla’s experience, because Franklin connected it to criticism he’d faced for decades.

He brought up his earlier work with Salt and said arguments about who could speak about Jesus were continuing across generations of artists.

GloRilla and Franklin have worked together on “Rain Down On Me” and “This Time,” putting her rap delivery alongside his gospel sound.

The latest pairing appears on Franklin’s I Am What I Am, which arrived October 30 with guests including Davido and Jelly Roll.

“Rain Down On Me” won the Dr. Bobby Jones Best Gospel/Inspirational Award at the 2025 BET Awards.

item.title: Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean Bring The Score To Miami Art Week
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean take their Fugees anniversary into Miami Art Week with a show and an audience-powered exhibit.
item.content:encoded:
Lauryn Hill is turning a Fugees anniversary into a Miami Art Week gathering where the music shares space with listeners’ own stories. She’s joining Wyclef Jean for a December 5 performance at Faena Forum in Miami Beach.

The set anchors The Fourth Space, a new Saint & Citizen event built around the 30th anniversary of The Score. Saint & Citizen’s event announcement pairs their performance with an exhibition tracing Black American and Haitian history, plus a short opening film.

That combination puts the people connected by the record alongside the artists who made it. “The Fourth Space is the one we create through shared culture, memory and experience,” Saint & Citizen CEO Paula Grant said in a statement quoted by Billboard.

The new booking follows Hill and Jean’s launch of the Fugees Hopeline, which invites callers to record personal reflections on hope. The artists’ original project announcement said selected recordings would enter an exhibition curated by Hill with Saint & Citizen.

That project gives listeners something to do beyond requesting their favorite record. Hill’s daughter Selah Marley narrates the phone experience, which also offers messages from the two artists and a new Fugees medley. The recordings are intended to grow into an international audio archive, giving ordinary callers a place in the anniversary alongside the group’s established history.

Hill has made visual work for the anniversary, too, creating three collages that combine archival photographs with typography. The images pull from three decades of the group’s history, extending the celebration beyond the songs people already know by heart.

The pair’s U.S. anniversary performances began November 4 at Berkeley’s Greek Theatre, with announced stops in Las Vegas, Los Angeles and Seattle. Miami adds an art-focused gathering to a celebration that’s already traveled through concert venues.

The organizer’s ticket page lists free exhibition admission from 2-5 P.M. Eastern on December 5, with separate tickets for the evening program. Kaytranada leads the after-party with opening sets from Joe Kay, giving attendees another reason to stay after Hill and Jean leave the stage.

The official ticket listing says the December 5 event is limited to attendees aged 21 and older.

item.title: Keith Sweat Brings Foster-Care Family Drama To Tubi With Fat Joe
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Keith Sweat steps into acting and executive production as Twin Pillars brings separated brothers and Fat Joe to Tubi.
item.content:encoded:
Keith Sweat is putting family separation on television with a new drama that brings Fat Joe into the cast. He’s both an executive producer and an actor in Twin Pillars: A Series, rather than simply lending his name to the credits.

The show’s official announcement identifies Darrin Dewitt Henson as its creator and director, with a November arrival on Tubi. At the center are fraternal twins whose parents’ incarceration sends them into foster care, leaving the brothers to grow into different lives.

Henson plays Dre opposite Alimi Ballard’s Maurice, while Sweat plays a club owner named Snow. Crystal Coney and Sean Anthony Baker also appear alongside Fat Joe.

“Music has always been my way of connecting with people through stories that speak to real-life experiences,” Keith Sweat said in a statement supplied to Billboard. The singer’s explanation places his television work alongside his music, with family and second chances driving this particular project.

Sweat already has a screen-producing credit beyond this new series. His official website lists him as an executive producer of The Secret Between Us, while also promoting the late-night radio program The Sweat Hotel.

Henson brings his own experience with family-centered television, including Soul Food and The Family Business. His career also runs through choreography, with a 2000 MTV Video Music Award for NSYNC’s “Bye Bye Bye” among his credits.

For Hip-Hop listeners, Sweat’s connection to Fat Joe isn’t coming out of nowhere. He’s also appeared on Joe and Jada, where Jadakiss recalled losing money to him during a studio dice game.

The television rollout comes with Sweat still keeping live dates on his calendar. His official schedule lists the Pompano Fall Festival in Deerfield Beach on November 28, followed by December appearances in Nigeria and South Africa.

The first three episodes of Twin Pillars are due on Tubi on November 16.

item.title: Kid Cudi Keeps Weed Off Movie Sets After 20-Blunt Days
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kid Cudi explains how he keeps weed away from work after a rehab stay, drawing a line between downtime and movie sets.
item.content:encoded:
Kid Cudi says movie sets and business meetings now come before marijuana, a change from the days when he estimates he smoked 15 to 20 blunts daily.

His latest account puts a workday boundary on a habit that once followed him everywhere.

During his Big Bro conversation with Travis Barker, released November 11, Cudi explained that his current smoking depends on his schedule.

On days with no obligations, he might smoke about four joints, but work means waiting until he gets home. “I’m not smoking at all during the day,” Cudi said.

His earlier public account also connected marijuana use to acting. In 2025, he described a sober movie performance as different from working while high, saying access to his emotions came more easily when he wasn’t smoking.

“If I was awake, I was smoking no matter what I was doing, right?” Cudi said.

He recalled carrying hundreds of pre-rolls in a Louis Vuitton briefcase, making the next smoke available before the previous one was finished.

His screen credits already included Don’t Look Up and How to Make It in America when he discussed that shift. The question for him wasn’t whether audiences enjoyed his performances, but how he felt while doing the work.

AllHipHop covered his earlier account of seeking help for marijuana use in August 2025, around the release of Cudi: The Memoir and his album Free. His book traced his Cleveland upbringing, music career and experiences with addiction and recovery.

Cudi said treatment changed his habits, though marijuana remains part of his life.

The exchange took place on a show where Cudi usually invites other people to open up. The two also revisited their early connection through Myspace and the MTV period of their careers.

Big Bro launched earlier this year with Kylie Jenner as its first guest, and Barker’s visit brought the host’s own habits into the discussion.

Later in the episode, Cudi said he also smokes cigarettes and wants to become more physically active.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Drake, Nicki Minaj & Lil Wayne Beat ‘Frivolous’ RICO Suit
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Drake, Nicki Minaj and Lil Wayne see a Michigan surveillance case dismissed after a judge finds no basis for the claims.
item.content:encoded:
Drake, Nicki Minaj and Lil Wayne have been dismissed from a Michigan lawsuit accusing Cash Money artists of turning secret surveillance of a woman’s life into music.

A federal judge rejected the allegations as frivolous, ending a case that also named Birdman, Slim and the label.

U.S. District Judge Judith E. Levy issued the dismissal order November 10 in Michigan’s Eastern District. The ruling came during the court’s required review of a complaint filed without prepayment of fees.

Levy wrote: “The Court concludes that Plaintiff’s complaint is frivolous because it lacks an arguable basis in fact or law.” The case was dismissed without prejudice, although Levy also concluded that another amendment would be futile.

Plaintiff Europe R. Colbert, representing herself, accused the defendants of placing surveillance equipment inside her Warren, Michigan home and using private information in recordings.

Those assertions were allegations in her complaint, which the judge rejected, rather than findings that any artist had engaged in surveillance.

Colbert invoked federal racketeering, wiretap and Lanham Act provisions alongside state claims, seeking damages and public corrections. Her amended complaint contained ten causes of action and also named Limp Bizkit among the defendants.

The initial complaint was dated September 28, followed by an amended version in early November.

The judge identified a missing piece of the paperwork behind the music accusations. Colbert referred to an attached list of allegedly infringing recordings, but Levy could not locate it.

Levy wrote: “But there is no Exhibit A attached to the amended complaint, original complaint, or anywhere else on the docket as far as the Court can discern.”

Levy evaluated the allegations under the screening rules for cases brought without upfront court fees. That review allows a judge to dismiss frivolous claims without treating every accusation as established fact.

Cash Money and Birdman also recently secured dismissal from a separate lawsuit over the shooting of Lil Wayne’s tour bus.

That Georgia case concerned a driver’s claims arising from the 2015 attack and was unrelated to Colbert’s Michigan complaint.

Levy additionally denied Colbert permission to appeal without prepaying fees, finding an appeal would not be taken in good faith.
